::: {.piege}
```{r}
NA == NA
NA * 0
NA^0
NA || TRUE
NA & FALSE
```
:::

## Why

`NA` means "unknown value". R returns `NA` when the result depends on that value, and a real result when it does not. Whatever the unknown number, its power 0 is 1, `unknown OR true` is true, and `unknown AND false` is false.

Conversely, `NA * 0` stays `NA`, because the unknown could be `Inf`, and `Inf * 0` is not 0. And `NA == NA` is `NA`: two unknowns are not necessarily equal. The rule is logical, but it means an `NA` can vanish from a calculation without leaving a trace.

## The remedy

Test for missing values explicitly with `is.na()`, rather than relying on their propagation.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
x <- c(3, NA, 5)
x == NA
is.na(x)
```
:::
